nations.name: Burns Paiute Tribe
nations.lands: Near Burns in Harney County, Oregon

facts.text: The Tribe’s strategic plan recounts that Wadatika ancestors were forcibly marched to the Yakama Reservation in Washington in 1878.
facts.evidence: forcibly marched to the Yakama Indian Reservation in Washington

facts.text: The Tribe recounts that Wadatika children kept speaking Paiute outside school after a small Tribal school opened in the 1920s.
facts.evidence: continued to use their Paiute language outside of school hours

facts.text: On October 13, 1972, Congress established the Burns Paiute Reservation in trust for the Burns Indian Colony.
facts.evidence: an Indian reservation for the use and benefit of said colony

facts.text: On February 2, 2017, the Tribal Council recognized a state of emergency for the Wadatika dialect of Northern Paiute and called for a language plan.

source.title: Burns Paiute Tribal Council Resolution No. 2017-03

facts.evidence: State of Emergency of the Wadatika Dialect
